definition: Maximum inner-product search (MIPS) is a search problem, with a corresponding class of search algorithms which attempt to maximise the inner product between a query and the data items to be retrieved.
details: MIPS algorithms are used in a wide variety of big data applications, including recommendation algorithms and machine learning. Formally, for a database of vectors x i {\displaystyle x_{i}} defined over a set of labels S {\displaystyle S} in an inner product space with an inner product ⟨ ⋅ , ⋅ ⟩ {\displaystyle \langle \cdot ,\cdot \rangle } defined on it, MIPS search can be defined as the problem of determining a r g m a x i ∈ S ⟨ x i , q ⟩ {\displaystyle {\underset {i\in S}{\operatorname {arg\,max} }}\ \langle x_{i},q\rangle } for a given query q {\displaystyle q} . Although there is an obvious linear-time implementation, it is generally too slow to be used on practical problems. However, efficient algorithms exist to speed up MIPS search. Under the assumption of all vectors in the set having constant norm, MIPS can be viewed as equivalent to a nearest neighbor search (NNS) problem in which maximizing the inner product is equivalent to minimizing the corresponding distance metric in the NNS problem. Like other forms of NNS, MIPS algorithms may be approximate or exact. MIPS search is used as part of DeepMind's RETRO algorithm.

explainer.lead: Maximum inner-product search (MIPS) is a search problem and a class of algorithms that maximise the inner product between a query and the data items to be retrieved. MIPS algorithms are used in big data applications including recommendation algorithms and machine learning.

tiers.eli5: Given a query, find the stored item that points most in the same direction and is longest in that direction, scored by multiplying matching components and adding them up.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use MIPS for retrieval over vector representations; a pitfall is that exact search over large databases is expensive, so approximate methods are needed.
tiers.paperLevel: For a database of vectors x_i over a label set S in an inner product space with inner product <.,.>, MIPS determines argmax over i in S of <x_i, q>.

explainer.example: A recommender stores user and item vectors and returns the item maximising <x_i, q> for the query vector q.
